task_3.title: Handle concurrent pytest cache directory creation without crashing
task_3.description: Pytest 8.2.2 fixes a regression in cache initialization so concurrent creation of the `.pytest_cache` directory, such as when using `pytest-xdist` together with `request.config.cache.mkdir(...)`, no longer aborts the run with a filesystem rename conflict. The change preserves normal cache creation behavior while continuing to surface unrelated filesystem errors.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that concurrent pytest runs creating cache directories do not fail when multiple processes initialize the shared cache at the same time.

expectation.grounded: When pytest initializes its cache and user code calls `request.config.cache.mkdir(...)`, concurrent processes attempting to establish the shared `.pytest_cache` directory must not fail with `OSError` caused by an `ENOTEMPTY` rename conflict if another process has already created or populated the target cache directory. Cache initialization should continue successfully in that race condition, while other rename-related `OSError` conditions must still be raised normally.
expectation.conceptual: Concurrent executions that touch pytest's cache should behave safely under contention. If one process loses the race to finalize the shared cache directory because another process already completed it, the run should continue instead of crashing; unrelated filesystem failures should still be reported.

constraints.grounded: The change is limited to the specific race where the cache directory rename fails with `ENOTEMPTY` during shared cache setup. Normal successful cache initialization must remain unchanged, and rename failures with any other error condition must preserve existing failure behavior.
constraints.conceptual: Only the known concurrent-cache race should be tolerated. The fix must not hide other filesystem problems or change successful cache setup semantics outside that race.

behavior: If two concurrent pytest processes both attempt to finalize the shared cache directory and one process encounters an `OSError` with `ENOTEMPTY` while renaming its temporary cache directory into place, pytest should suppress that conflict and continue startup.
When the cache directory rename succeeds normally, pytest should preserve its existing cache initialization flow.
If the cache directory rename fails for any reason other than the specific concurrent `ENOTEMPTY` conflict, pytest should continue to raise the original error.
acceptance_criteria: When a session-scoped fixture uses `request.config.cache.mkdir(...)` and tests run concurrently against the same project cache, pytest should complete startup without failing solely because another process created the shared cache directory first.
When concurrent cache initialization triggers a rename conflict whose observable error condition is `ENOTEMPTY`, pytest should not abort the run with that error.
When cache directory initialization encounters a different rename-related filesystem error, pytest should still fail and surface that error to the user.
When no concurrent cache race occurs, cache directory setup should behave the same as before the fix.

task_2.title: Restore prompt cleanup of unittest test instances
task_2.description: Pytest 8.2.2 fixes a regression introduced in 8.2.x where instances created for unittest-based tests were retained until session teardown instead of being released when each test finished. The update restores prompt teardown cleanup for unittest.TestCase items so per-test objects and their attached state do not stay alive longer than expected.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that pytest releases each `unittest.TestCase` instance at test teardown, rather than retaining it until session teardown, so per-test state is cleaned up promptly after each test completes.

expectation.grounded: When pytest executes `unittest.TestCase` methods through its unittest integration, `TestCaseFunction` teardown should clear the stored references to the executed test object and its instance once teardown finishes. Any explicit unittest teardown hook associated with the item should still run before those references are dropped. This restores the pre-regression behavior for unittest-backed tests in pytest 8.2.2.
expectation.conceptual: Pytest should treat each unittest-based test as a short-lived object: once the test and its teardown are done, the framework should stop holding references to that test instance so its state can be released immediately instead of lingering for the rest of the session.

constraints.grounded: The fix is scoped to pytest's `unittest.TestCase` handling and should preserve normal teardown execution order. This release should not broaden lifecycle changes to regular pytest test functions or non-unittest test classes.
constraints.conceptual: Keep the change limited to the unittest integration and avoid altering teardown behavior for other kinds of pytest tests.

behavior: For `unittest.TestCase` tests run by pytest, the per-test instance is no longer retained until session teardown and is released during item teardown.
Cleanup still includes any explicit unittest teardown logic before pytest drops its stored references to the executed test object.
Large or expensive state attached to a unittest test instance is no longer kept alive solely because pytest continues to reference that instance after the test has finished.
The 8.2.2 fix is specific to unittest-backed tests and does not change retention semantics for ordinary pytest `Function` items in this update.
acceptance_criteria: When a `unittest.TestCase` test method completes under pytest, the instance created for that method should become eligible for release as part of that test's teardown rather than only at the end of the test session.
When a `unittest.TestCase` instance stores expensive state during setup or execution, that state should not remain reachable solely because pytest keeps the test instance referenced after teardown.
When multiple `unittest.TestCase` methods run in one session, each method should still use its own per-test instance and that instance should be released after its teardown completes.
When running non-unittest pytest tests, upgrading to 8.2.2 should not introduce additional teardown lifecycle changes as part of this fix.

task_1.title: Prevent collection slowdowns for high-scope parametrized tests
task_1.description: Pytest 8.2.2 fixes a collection-time bug where certain uses of @pytest.mark.parametrize with many parameters and a higher scope could cause pathological slowdown or apparent hangs during test collection. The upgrade preserves normal parametrization behavior while preventing redundant item reordering work.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that test collection does not hang or degrade catastrophically when users apply `@pytest.mark.parametrize` with many parameter names and set the parametrization scope to `"module"` or `"session"`.

expectation.grounded: When collecting tests that use `pytest.mark.parametrize` with a large set of argument names and higher-than-function scope, pytest should complete collection normally instead of spending excessive time in collection-time reordering. The public parametrization API and the resulting collected test items should remain valid, unique, and executable under `scope="module"` and `scope="session"`.
expectation.conceptual: Higher-scoped parametrized tests with many parameters should collect in a practical amount of time and behave like normal parametrized tests, rather than appearing to hang during collection.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the public `pytest.mark.parametrize` interface or the intended grouping behavior for higher-scoped parametrized items. The fix should avoid redundant reordering side effects so that collection still yields the same logical set of tests without duplicate execution.
constraints.conceptual: Keep existing parametrization behavior intact while removing the collection-time performance failure. Users should not need to change how they declare parametrized tests.

behavior: A test function parametrized over many argument names in a single `pytest.mark.parametrize` call no longer causes catastrophic collection slowdown merely because the parametrization scope is `"module"` or `"session"`.
Collection-time reordering for higher-scoped parametrized items should reprioritize items without repeatedly re-adding the same collected item in a way that causes pathological performance growth.
The collected test set remains logically unchanged: parametrized cases are still collected and run once each, using the existing higher-scope parametrization semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Given a test function with many parameter names in one `@pytest.mark.parametrize(..., scope="module")`, when pytest collects the suite, then collection should complete normally and the generated parametrized cases should execute once each.

Given a test function with many parameter names in one `@pytest.mark.parametrize(..., scope="session")`, when pytest collects the suite, then collection should complete normally rather than appearing to hang during collection.

When the same collected item participates in reordering across multiple higher-scoped parameter keys, pytest should still produce the same logical set of collected tests without duplicate execution or runaway collection-time slowdown.

task_6.title: Add canonical stable URLs to generated documentation
task_6.description: Pytest 8.2.2 updates its generated documentation pages to declare the stable docs site as the canonical source, reducing the chance that users land on outdated or temporary documentation URLs from search results.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that generated documentation pages identify the stable pytest documentation as the canonical source so users are directed to current docs instead of outdated versioned pages in search results.

expectation.grounded: The pytest documentation build should publish HTML pages with a canonical URL rooted at `https://docs.pytest.org/en/stable/` via the Sphinx `html_baseurl` setting, so documentation consumers and search engines can associate older or alternate-hosted pages with the stable documentation version.
expectation.conceptual: Published documentation should consistently signal that the stable documentation site is the authoritative location for each page, improving discoverability of current docs without changing pytest runtime behavior.

constraints.grounded: This change is limited to documentation site metadata and must not alter pytest APIs, command behavior, warning behavior, error behavior, or the visible documentation content apart from canonical link metadata emitted in generated HTML.
constraints.conceptual: The update should only improve how documentation pages are identified by external indexers and readers; it must not introduce functional changes to the library itself or otherwise change what users read on the docs pages.

behavior: Generated documentation HTML pages now expose the stable documentation site as their canonical base URL.
Older documentation versions and alternate hosted copies can be associated with the stable docs location by consumers that honor canonical links.
The library's runtime semantics remain unchanged because the update only affects documentation page metadata.
acceptance_criteria: When pytest documentation is built and published, each HTML page should declare the stable docs site as its canonical source.

When a search engine or other consumer reads the published docs metadata, it should be able to identify the stable documentation URL as the preferred page location over older or alternate-hosted versions.
When upgrading from 8.2.1 to 8.2.2, pytest execution and public library behavior should remain unchanged.

task_4.title: Enable dark mode on the documentation site
task_4.description: The documentation website was moved from the previous Flask-based Sphinx theme to Furo so the published docs support dark mode and use the newer sidebar layout, without changing pytest runtime behavior.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the documentation website supports a dark theme and presents the updated navigation/sidebar experience introduced in version 8.2.2, while leaving pytest's runtime behavior unchanged.

expectation.grounded: Sphinx HTML documentation should use the `furo` theme instead of the previous `flask` theme so that the docs site exposes dark-mode styling. The rendered sidebar should use Furo-compatible brand, search, scroll, navigation, relation, links, and style controls for the index page and general documentation pages.
expectation.conceptual: The published documentation should offer a built-in light/dark viewing experience and a modernized sidebar layout that remains easy to navigate across the site.

constraints.grounded: This change is limited to HTML documentation presentation. It should not alter pytest APIs, command behavior, collection, execution, warnings, exceptions, or other library runtime semantics. Existing documentation content and navigability should remain available under the new theme.
constraints.conceptual: The update should only affect how the documentation site looks and feels. It must not introduce behavioral changes to the library itself or reduce access to normal documentation content and navigation.

behavior: The documentation site renders with the Furo Sphinx theme rather than the prior Flask-based theme.
Users can view the documentation in a dark theme as part of the site theme experience.
The sidebar layout is updated to the Furo-style structure, including branded header elements, search, navigation sections, and theme/style controls.
The documentation homepage and internal pages use sidebar configurations appropriate to their page type while preserving access to documentation links and table-of-contents navigation.
The library's runtime behavior is unaffected because the change is confined to documentation generation and presentation.
acceptance_criteria: When a user opens the published documentation, it should provide a dark-mode viewing option as part of the site theme.
When documentation pages are rendered, they should use the updated Furo visual style instead of the previous Flask-based appearance.
When a user navigates the homepage or internal documentation pages, they should still have access to search, navigation links, and related documentation links through the updated sidebar.
When upgrading from 8.2.1 to 8.2.2, users should not observe any change in pytest runtime APIs or execution behavior attributable to this update.

task_5.title: Document pytest thread-safety limits for flaky warning capture
task_5.description: Pytest 8.2.2 clarifies in its user documentation that pytest is not thread-safe and that concurrent use of warning-capture helpers such as pytest.warns can cause flaky behavior because they rely on Python's non-thread-safe warning capture machinery. The update is explanatory and does not introduce a runtime fix.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the upgrade documentation clearly warns users that pytest is not thread-safe and that multithreaded use of warning-capture helpers such as pytest.warns may lead to flaky results rather than deterministic behavior.

expectation.grounded: The upgrade should document that pytest's flaky-test guidance includes lack of thread safety as a possible source of intermittent failures, and that pytest.warns inherits the thread-safety limitations of warnings.catch_warnings. Users should understand that concurrent warning capture across threads can behave unreliably and that version 8.2.2 is clarifying this limitation, not adding a thread-safe guarantee.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be explicitly told that running pytest features concurrently across threads, especially warning capture, can cause flaky outcomes because those operations are not thread-safe. This release should be understood as a documentation clarification of existing behavior rather than a behavioral fix.

constraints.grounded: Do not imply that pytest.warns, warnings.catch_warnings integration, or pytest generally became thread-safe in 8.2.2. Preserve the existing runtime semantics and frame the update as documentation of a known limitation affecting threaded execution.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade must set expectations about an existing concurrency limitation without suggesting that threaded pytest usage is now reliable or changed at runtime.

behavior: Flaky-test guidance now identifies pytest's lack of thread safety as a possible cause of intermittent failures.
Concurrent use of pytest.warns in multiple threads is documented as potentially flaky because it depends on Python warning capture behavior that is not thread-safe.
The update adds user-facing clarification only and does not introduce new runtime guarantees for threaded pytest execution.
acceptance_criteria: When users consult the upgraded flaky-test debugging guidance, it should explicitly mention pytest's lack of thread safety as a possible source of flakiness.
When users rely on pytest.warns from multiple threads, the documented expectation should be that intermittent failures may occur because warning capture is not thread-safe.
The upgrade messaging should make clear that 8.2.2 documents an existing limitation rather than claiming a runtime fix for threaded warning capture.
